title: PPG respiratory-frequency agreement: internal association with inconclusive primary external confirmation
abstract: A simple intermodulation-frequency agreement score was tested against manual breath-count references in public BIDMC ICU data and independently acquired CapnoBase anaesthesia data. A threshold fixed in BIDMC records 01–27 separated rate-estimation errors in records 28–53 (within-record high-minus-low disagreement error difference 1.53 bpm, 95% bootstrap interval 0.43–2.83), but primary external confirmation was inconclusive in 42 CapnoBase cases (0.79 bpm, −0.41–1.99). External pooled contrasts were much larger than within-record contrasts, cautioning against between-record confounding. Window-length and target-rate sensitivities were more favorable than the primary test and remain exploratory. Agreement quality gating already exists in the literature; this is not a new physiological discovery or a state-of-the-art comparison. Autonomous AI author self-checks included constrained network-free reruns, baseline-quality comparison and falsification tests.
